about: Hand-researched outcomes for finished ALS studies, used by scripts/fetch-registry.mjs. Keyed by NCT ID. verdict is one of: Met primary endpoint, Missed primary endpoint, No benefit shown (exploratory study with no formal primary endpoint), Mixed results, Inconclusive, Stopped: no benefit, Stopped: safety, Stopped: slow enrollment, Stopped: business or funding, Extension or access study, Safety study, Descriptive results (no comparison or formal test, e.g. a feasibility or physiology study), Not a treatment study, No results found. summary says what happened in plain words; source is the checked publication or report it rests on (null only for facts that are part of the registry record itself or widely documented, e.g. a drug's market withdrawal). ignorePublications: true hides publications the registry links as results when they are really background or a different study. Studies not listed here get an automatic outcome from the registry (its stop reason, posted results and linked publications).

NCT00021697.summary: Dextromethorphan/quinidine (AVP-923) reduced pseudobulbar affect (uncontrolled laughing or crying) more than either drug alone. A symptom treatment, not a disease-slowing one.

NCT00573443.summary: Dextromethorphan/quinidine reduced pseudobulbar affect episodes in people with ALS or MS; this trial supported the drug's approval (Nuedexta) for pseudobulbar affect.

NCT00386464.summary: Crossover trial of starting night-time non-invasive ventilation early, in patients with mild breathing involvement. No results were posted or found in a literature search.

NCT00047723.summary: Minocycline did not help and appeared harmful: function declined about 25% faster on minocycline than on placebo.

NCT00035815.summary: Two years of subcutaneous IGF-1 gave no benefit on muscle strength compared with placebo.

NCT00125203.summary: In 20 patients, botulinum toxin B injected into the salivary glands reduced drooling for about four weeks without significant side effects. A symptom treatment.

NCT00136110.summary: Valproate did not improve survival or slow functional decline in 163 patients.

NCT00353665.summary: Memantine showed no effect on functional decline over 12 months in 63 patients; the trial was small, so a modest effect could not be ruled out.

NCT00330681.summary: Edaravone's first phase 3 missed its primary endpoint across all patients. A post hoc analysis pointed to earlier, more typical patients, which the later MCI186-19 trial tested and confirmed.

NCT00349622.summary: Despite an early signal, the phase 3 stage (513 patients) found no slowing of functional decline, and ceftriaxone caused more gallbladder and liver problems (12% vs 0% on placebo).

NCT00372879.summary: Small crossover trial of high-dose vitamin E for muscle cramps. No results were posted or found.

NCT00415519.summary: Exploratory study in 25 patients with more advanced ALS (Japanese severity grade 3): function declined about equally on edaravone and placebo.

NCT00424463.summary: Double-blind extension of edaravone's first phase 3, testing whether continued treatment sustained any effect; published as exploratory.

NCT01492686.summary: In patients selected for early, typically progressing ALS, IV edaravone slowed functional decline by about a third over 24 weeks. This trial led to FDA approval (Radicava) in 2017.

NCT04577404.summary: Open-label safety study of oral edaravone in 185 patients: no new safety concerns over 48 weeks. It supported FDA approval of the oral form (Radicava ORS) in 2022.

NCT04569084.summary: Tested whether daily oral edaravone beats the approved on/off schedule. Stopped in 2023 when an interim analysis showed no difference (futility).

NCT05568615.summary: Open-label safety extension of oral edaravone in Japan (15 patients), run until the drug was on the market there.

NCT05178810.summary: Ferrer's oral edaravone (FAB122) did not slow functional decline over 48 weeks, and showed no survival benefit; it was safe.

NCT00444613.summary: Ultra-high-dose methylcobalamin (vitamin B12) missed both primary endpoints (time to death or ventilation, and function). A post hoc look at patients enrolled within a year of onset suggested benefit, which led to the JETALS trial.

NCT00445172.summary: Long-term open-label extension of Eisai's methylcobalamin trial.

NCT03548311.summary: JETALS: in patients enrolled within a year of onset and with moderate progression, ultra-high-dose methylcobalamin slowed functional decline over 16 weeks compared with placebo.

NCT00833820.summary: Small sham-controlled trial of magnetic stimulation of the motor cortex. A Cochrane review of the rTMS trials in ALS found no clear benefit over sham.

NCT00706147.summary: Small trial (36 patients) in rapidly progressing SOD1-ALS: arimoclomol was safe, and survival and function trended its way without reaching significance. The planned phase 3 part was dropped because recruitment was slow.

NCT03491462.summary: ORARIALS-01: arimoclomol missed its primary endpoint (function and survival combined) and all secondary endpoints over 76 weeks in 245 patients.

NCT00868166.summary: Olesoxime gave no survival benefit at 18 months (69% vs 68% alive) in 512 patients taking riluzole.

NCT01285583.summary: Open-label safety extension of the olesoxime phase 3, which showed no benefit.

NCT00965497.summary: Small open-label study (13 patients) of escitalopram for depression in people with ALS or MS. No results were posted or found.

NCT01016522.summary: Safety study of a ketogenic tube-feed diet. Only one patient enrolled, and the study was stopped for low enrollment.

NCT00876772.summary: Olanzapine for appetite loss and weight loss. No published results were found; the EU trials register lists a results section.

NCT01281189.summary: EMPOWER: dexpramipexole had no effect on function or survival in 943 patients, and Biogen ended its development in ALS.

NCT01933321.summary: Open-label study of the patient's own blood stem cells given into the spinal fluid (14 patients). No results were posted or found.

NCT01583088.summary: Stopped early: patients given diaphragm pacing with ventilation died sooner than those on ventilation alone. Diaphragm pacing is not recommended in ALS.

NCT01160263.summary: Brain imaging (SPECT) study, not a treatment trial.

NCT01825551.summary: Five days of G-CSF did not slow progression over 3 months in 40 patients; women given G-CSF declined faster than those on placebo.

NCT01776970.summary: CANALS: nabiximols (THC/CBD mouth spray) reduced spasticity over 6 weeks in 59 patients with ALS or primary lateral sclerosis. A symptom treatment; the authors called for larger trials.

NCT02588677.summary: Masitinib met its primary endpoint in the prespecified 'normal progressor' group (27% slower decline over 48 weeks) but not across all patients. It has not been approved, and a confirmatory phase 3 was required.

NCT01994109.summary: RimabotulinumtoxinB (Myobloc) reduced drooling compared with placebo in 187 adults with drooling from several causes; 12 had ALS.

NCT02496767.summary: VITALITY-ALS: tirasemtiv did not slow the decline in breathing capacity, and many patients stopped it because of side effects (34% vs 12% on placebo).

NCT02936635.summary: Open-label extension of tirasemtiv; development stopped after VITALITY-ALS failed.

NCT02623699.summary: VALOR: tofersen did not significantly slow functional decline at 28 weeks, but it sharply lowered SOD1 and neurofilament light, a marker of nerve damage. On that biomarker evidence it received FDA accelerated approval (Qalsody) in 2023.

NCT03070119.summary: Open-label extension of VALOR. Patients who started tofersen earlier declined less by 52 weeks than those who started later (exploratory).

NCT03068754.summary: PENNANT: stopped in 2019 because more patients developed pneumonia on Acthar Gel than on placebo, and too few had reached the endpoint to judge efficacy.

NCT03280056.summary: NurOwn (MSC-NTF cells): 34.7% of treated patients responded vs 27.7% on placebo, not a significant difference. FDA advisers later voted against approval.

NCT03505021.summary: REFALS: oral levosimendan did not slow the decline in breathing capacity at 12 weeks, nor overall function, in 496 patients.

NCT03293069.summary: FAIR-ALS II: deferiprone (iron chelation) vs placebo over 12 months. No results were posted or found in a search in November 2026.

NCT04436510.summary: HEALEY Regimen B: verdiperstat showed no difference from placebo on disease progression.

NCT04436497.summary: HEALEY Regimen A: zilucoplan was stopped early for futility, with no meaningful slowing of progression.

NCT04414345.summary: HEALEY Regimen C: CNM-Au8 missed its primary and secondary endpoints at 24 weeks. Exploratory analyses suggested longer survival at the 30 mg dose, which the RESTORE-ALS phase 3 is designed to test.

NCT04615923.summary: HEALEY Regimen D: pridopidine had no effect on functional decline over 24 weeks. Later analyses in faster-progressing patients led to the PREVAiLS phase 3.

NCT05136885.summary: HEALEY Regimen E: IV trehalose (SLS-005) missed its primary endpoint overall; a prespecified subgroup not taking AMX0035 declined 22% more slowly.

NCT05740813.summary: HEALEY Regimen F: fosigotifator (ABBV-CLS-7262) missed its primary and secondary endpoints.

NCT05842941.summary: HEALEY Regimen G: DNL343 missed its primary endpoint (function and survival) at 24 weeks.

NCT04516096.summary: Compassionate-use access to AMX0035 for patients who finished earlier Amylyx trials; no efficacy comparison.

NCT05619783.summary: Open-label extension of the PHOENIX phase 3. PHOENIX missed its primary endpoint, and Amylyx withdrew AMX0035 (Relyvrio) from the market in 2024.

NCT04745299.summary: ALSUMMIT: lenzumestrocel (Neuronata-R stem cells) missed its primary endpoint (function and survival) in the overall population. The company reports post hoc benefit in slower-progressing patients.

NCT04944784.summary: COURAGE-ALS: stopped for futility at a planned interim analysis; reldesemtiv did not slow functional decline.

NCT06111014.summary: Continuation study of latozinemab, stopped after its parent phase 3 in frontotemporal dementia due to GRN mutations (INFRONT-3) missed its clinical endpoint.

NCT03766321.summary: Placebo-controlled trial of faecal microbiota transplantation (42 patients). No results posted; the papers the registry links are background reading, not this trial's results.

NCT05189106.summary: Open-label basket study of baricitinib in 9 people with ALS and 7 with Alzheimer's: the drug reached the spinal fluid; one serious adverse event in the ALS group. No efficacy comparison.

NCT05163886.summary: Small safety study (15 patients with C9orf72 ALS), placebo-controlled for 12 weeks: 9 of 10 completed treatment on LAM-002A. Not designed to test efficacy.

NCT05039099.summary: Phase 2a safety study in 73 patients with sporadic or SOD1 ALS: no anti-drug antibodies; serious adverse events in 19 of 66 people given AP-101 (including open-label treatment) vs 7 of 25 on placebo. Not designed to test efficacy.

NCT04490148.summary: Home breathing tests flagged the need for ventilation a median of 176 days after enrolment, vs 259 days with clinic tests (34 patients; no formal comparison).

NCT04866771.summary: Pilot (14 patients): less functional decline was reported during transcranial direct current stimulation than in the delayed-start group, without a statistical test.

NCT04499963.summary: Open-label (50 treated): the rate of functional decline on Theracurmin was no different from the comparison group (p=0.98).

NCT06429059.summary: Pilot (50 patients) assigning supplements by genomic subtype: no difference in functional decline between approaches (p=0.56).

NCT05542576.summary: Retinal tracer AMDX-2011P in 13 people: a few mild side effects at the higher doses; no serious adverse events.

NCT05979688.summary: Small trial of yogic breathing exercise. No results posted; the paper the registry links is a different study.

NCT04998305.summary: Small crossover trial (11 patients): muscle-cramp scores were similar on TJ-68 and placebo.

NCT04245709.summary: Open-label (25 patients): two serious adverse events on clenbuterol; no control group to judge efficacy.

NCT06889857.summary: Open-label study of a stem-cell-derived secretome (8 patients). No results posted; the paper the registry links is a different trial (JETALS).

NCT04632225.summary: 18 patients: Engensis injections into muscle were generally tolerated (bruising, fever); one serious adverse event on Engensis.

NCT04953286.summary: Study of tear fluid chemistry in ALS; published in 2024.

NCT05039268.summary: 16 patients: no serious or severe adverse events; a PET measure of motor-cortex inflammation did not change after 7 days (only 8 scanned).

NCT05508074.summary: 51 patients with bulbar-onset ALS on riluzole: more side effects on IFB-088 (25 of 34 vs 10 of 17); serious adverse events 8 of 34 vs 4 of 17. A safety-focused phase 2.

NCT04322149.summary: Open-label dose study (54 patients) of AT-1501 (tegoprubart): generally tolerated, with one serious adverse event across four doses.

NCT05003167.summary: Single-group study (13 patients): expiratory muscle training raised maximum expiratory pressure from 66 to 84 cmH2O (p=0.001).

NCT05176093.summary: Six-month extension of the Engensis safety study (8 patients).

NCT03427086.summary: Small placebo-controlled safety study of high-dose biotin (12 patients). No results posted; the papers the registry links are general reviews.

NCT04176224.summary: Pharmacology study: measured blood levels of oral edaravone in 9 patients.

NCT04254913.summary: Pharmacology study: measured blood levels of oral edaravone given through a feeding tube in 6 patients.

NCT02118727.summary: Memantine 20 mg twice daily did not slow functional decline over 36 weeks (−0.29 vs −0.28 points a week, 89 patients).

NCT03487263.summary: Phase 1b dose-escalation and safety study of the anti-CD14 antibody IC14 in 10 patients; published in 2021.

NCT03411863.summary: Physiology study of cervical spinal stimulation in 11 people with ALS and 8 controls; not a test of treatment benefit.

NCT03851302.summary: Physiology study of remote ischaemic conditioning with hand exercise, mostly in spinal cord injury (2 people with ALS).

NCT03883581.summary: Open-label (28 patients): no significant change in swallowing safety, speech intelligibility or patient-rated bulbar function after 30 days of Nuedexta (p=0.08 to 0.65).

NCT03506425.summary: Open-label pilot (15 patients): decline slowed from 0.57 to 0.39 points a month on triheptanoin, not statistically significant (p=0.32).

NCT03986671.summary: Test of a throat EMG probe: readings agreed in 78% of people with ALS vs 96% of healthy volunteers.

NCT03488524.summary: Open-label extension of CENTAUR (90 patients). Published analyses linked longer survival to earlier AMX0035, but the PHOENIX phase 3 later failed and the drug was withdrawn in 2024.

NCT04055623.summary: Small randomised trial (11 patients; enrolment cut short by COVID-19) of regulatory T-cell infusions with IL-2; Treg function was measured, with no efficacy conclusion. The paper the registry links is the earlier phase 1.

NCT03214224.summary: Home breathing tests gave values close to clinic tests (FVC 80% vs 73% predicted) in 40 patients.

NCT03694132.summary: Brain-imaging and EEG/MEG study of sensory-motor pathways in ALS; published in 2025.

NCT04098406.summary: RESCUE-ALS: CNM-Au8 missed its primary nerve-conduction (EMG) endpoint (p=0.43) in 45 patients; exploratory clinical measures were reported in the publication.

NCT03645031.summary: Single-session physiology study (14 people with ALS, 11 controls) of brief low-oxygen breathing; no consistent improvement in breathing strength in ALS.

NCT02437110.summary: Phase 1: a four-drug antiretroviral regimen lowered HERV-K levels by about 31% over 24 weeks; no serious adverse events. Clinical benefit was not tested here (that was Lighthouse II).

NCT03293394.summary: Real transcranial direct current stimulation with rehabilitation improved muscle strength at 2 weeks compared with sham (p=0.001, 30 patients).

NCT03168711.summary: Raising urate with inosine (23 patients): 12 of 14 on inosine and 7 of 9 on placebo completed; serious adverse events 4 vs 1.

NCT03472950.summary: Open-label (14 patients): dose-limiting side effects in 1 of 6 at 500 mg and 2 of 8 at 1000 mg of ranolazine; no serious adverse events.

NCT02447952.summary: Feasibility of a wearable sensor (25 patients): it was worn about 12 hours a day.

NCT02469896.summary: Pilot (22 patients): tolerability of tocilizumab similar to placebo; no deaths. Not designed to test efficacy.

NCT03127514.summary: CENTAUR: AMX0035 slowed functional decline (−1.24 vs −1.66 points a month, p=0.03) in 137 fast-progressing patients. It was approved in 2022, but the confirmatory PHOENIX trial failed and it was withdrawn in 2024.

NCT02891629.summary: Feasibility of the EyeControl eye-tracking communication device in 5 people with ALS and 10 volunteers.

NCT02682030.summary: Only 5 patients enrolled and 2 completed, too few to compare the airway-clearance devices.

NCT03160898.summary: FORTITUDE-ALS: reldesemtiv did not significantly slow the decline in breathing capacity at 12 weeks (p=0.11), though trends favoured it; the phase 3 COURAGE-ALS that followed was stopped for futility.

NCT02872142.summary: Open-label (12 patients) plasma exchange with albumin; no control group.

NCT02059759.summary: IMODALS (36 patients): low-dose IL-2 raised regulatory T-cell numbers, its primary (biomarker) endpoint, and was well tolerated; this led to the MIROCALS trial.

NCT03241784.summary: Phase 1 (3 patients): no treatment-related adverse events from regulatory T-cell infusions.

NCT02781454.summary: In 20 patients, mexiletine changed a measure of motor-nerve excitability (resting motor threshold) compared with placebo (p=0.04). A drug-effect study, not a test of disease progression.

NCT03456882.summary: RNS60 had no effect on the primary blood biomarkers of inflammation over 24 weeks (147 patients).

NCT02709330.summary: Open-label (50 patients) compared with historical controls: lunasin did not change the rate of decline (p=0.99).

NCT02525471.summary: Open-label (16 patients): 13 completed 24 weeks of RNS60; one serious adverse event.

NCT02789059.summary: Study of muscle oxygen use during effort in neuromuscular diseases.

NCT02418546.summary: Weight held steady with in-person (−0.1 kg) or app-based (−0.2 kg) nutrition counselling, vs −1.2 kg with standard care over 6 months (78 patients; no formal test).

NCT02714036.summary: Open-label (35 patients): ibudilast did not change a PET measure of brain inflammation after 12 to 24 weeks.

NCT03039673.summary: MIROCALS (304 patients): low-dose IL-2 did not improve survival overall, the primary endpoint; a prespecified analysis suggested benefit in patients with lower spinal-fluid neurofilament levels.

NCT02450552.summary: Drug-effect study (65 patients) of ezogabine on motor-neuron excitability measured by magnetic stimulation; results are posted on the registry.

NCT02670226.summary: Study of muscle metabolism in early ALS; published in 2022.

NCT02460679.summary: Open-label (19 patients): no drug-related serious adverse events on EPI-589.

NCT02017912.summary: Phase 2 of NurOwn (48 patients): serious adverse events in 8 of 36 treated vs 1 of 12 on placebo. The phase 3 that followed missed its primary endpoint.

NCT01709149.summary: BENEFIT-ALS: tirasemtiv did not improve function at 12 weeks (p=0.11; numerically worse) in 711 patients, though breathing capacity declined less, which led to the VITALITY-ALS phase 3.

NCT01786174.summary: Short phase 2a (30 patients, 8 weeks): fingolimod was tolerated, with no difference from placebo in function or breathing.

NCT01806857.summary: Crossover trial: Nuedexta improved patient-rated bulbar function (speech, swallowing, saliva) compared with placebo (p=0.0003). A symptom treatment.

NCT02039401.summary: Open-label (18 patients): VM202 injections into muscle were generally tolerated; three serious adverse events.

NCT01906658.summary: Dose-finding safety study of Acthar Gel (43 patients): 4 had side effects that required stopping or could not be controlled.

NCT01232738.summary: Open-label (36 patients) compared with historical placebo data: decline on rasagiline was slightly faster (−1.20 vs −0.94 points a month, p=0.07).

NCT04947436.summary: Small comparison (28 patients) of airway-clearance devices; respiratory-complication scores were similar and no formal analysis was possible.

NCT01884571.summary: Open-label combination immunosuppression (31 patients): no one met the target improvement in function.

NCT02288091.summary: Open-label (25 patients): 24 completed 12 weeks of inosine; three serious adverse events.

NCT03828123.summary: Open-label study of the patient's own mesenchymal stem cells (26 patients). No results posted; the paper the registry links is an earlier trial.

NCT01640067.summary: Phase 1 (18 patients) of neural stem-cell transplantation into the spinal cord; published in 2015.

NCT01823380.summary: Low vitamin D levels were associated with more severe ALS in 127 patients (published 2020).

NCT01786603.summary: Rasagiline did not significantly slow functional decline over 12 months (80 patients).

NCT01753076.summary: Ozanezumab did not improve function or survival (p=0.12; numerically worse) in 304 patients.

NCT01849770.summary: Phase 2 (60 patients): mexiletine 900 mg a day was poorly tolerated (32% stopped) vs 5% at 300 mg. Not powered for efficacy.

NCT02238626.summary: Phase 2 (70 patients): ibudilast with riluzole was generally tolerated. It led to the COMBAT-ALS phase 2b/3.

NCT02479802.summary: Open-label (13 patients) plasma exchange with albumin: function and breathing declined over 48 weeks; no control group.

NCT01811355.summary: Crossover trial (23 patients): mexiletine reduced how often and how badly muscle cramps occurred, compared with placebo. A symptom treatment.

NCT02164253.summary: FAIR-ALS pilot (23 patients): deferiprone was safe, and decline was smaller in the first 3 months of treatment. It led to FAIR-ALS II.

NCT00877604.summary: TUDCA (34 patients): more responders by rate of decline over a year (13 of 15 vs 6 of 14 on placebo). A larger phase 3 followed.

NCT00326625.summary: Glatiramer acetate did not slow functional decline over 52 weeks (366 patients, p=0.48).

NCT00243932.summary: High-dose coenzyme Q10 was judged not promising enough for a phase 3 (futility design, 185 patients).

NCT02880033.summary: Study of ferroptosis-related blood markers alongside deferiprone; published in 2019.

NCT01089010.summary: Phase 2a of tirasemtiv (67 patients): safety and early drug effects; published in 2012.

NCT00600873.summary: Early-phase study of high-dose R(+)pramipexole (dexpramipexole) in 10 patients; published in 2008.

NCT00647296.summary: Phase 2 of dexpramipexole: well tolerated, with a dose-related trend toward slower decline that led to the EMPOWER phase 3, which failed.

NCT01154283.summary: Crossover trial (28 patients): ventilator use was similar with standard bi-level and inspiratory-only settings.

NCT00790582.summary: Open-label lithium (109 patients) compared with historical controls: decline was not slower (1.20 vs 1.01 points a month).

NCT01083667.summary: Open-label (32 patients with SOD1-ALS): tested whether pyrimethamine lowers SOD1 in spinal fluid; results are posted on the registry.

NCT01363401.summary: Repeated injections of the patient's own stem cells (lenzumestrocel): function declined less at 16 weeks than without treatment (−1.4 vs −4.7 points; 72 patients, open-label control). The ALSUMMIT phase 3 later missed its primary endpoint.

NCT01123148.summary: Brain-computer interface for wheelchair tilt: typing accuracy stayed about 91% while tilting; tested in able-bodied volunteers only.

NCT01123200.summary: In-home brain-computer interface (1 participant), used for 5 months.

NCT00931944.summary: Long-term open-label extension of dexpramipexole (74 patients).

NCT01257581.summary: Selection design comparing creatine and two doses of tamoxifen (60 patients): rates of decline were similar (−0.74 to −0.98 points a month); no placebo group.

NCT00983983.summary: Pilot in 24 patients with feeding tubes: the high-carbohydrate, high-calorie diet was the best tolerated, with fewer serious adverse events than the control diet.

NCT00860951.summary: Brain-computer interface keyboard: about 85% typing accuracy across settings (29 participants).

NCT01378676.summary: Repeated-dose safety study of tirasemtiv (49 patients); published in 2013.

NCT00613899.summary: Home, on-demand mechanical cough assistance with telesurveillance (40 patients); published in 2010.

NCT01119001.summary: Brain-computer interface keyboard used by 13 people with ALS: about 81% typing accuracy.

NCT00116558.summary: Early ventilation and nutrition study (153 patients): 35 accepted early non-invasive ventilation; design and early results published in 2011.

NCT05981040.summary: Usnoflast (ZYIL1), 24 patients over 12 weeks: no significant difference from placebo; the 75 mg group was numerically better on function (about 2.8 points). Well tolerated.

NCT05357950.summary: PARADIGM (68 patients): PrimeC was safe, its primary endpoint. Function at 6 months was not significantly better (2.2 points, p=0.12), but patients on PrimeC throughout were 7.9 points better at 18 months (p=0.007). Not powered for efficacy; a confirmatory trial is planned.

NCT04788745.summary: Open-label (21 patients): trimetazidine was safe and well tolerated, and lowered a marker of oxidative stress and resting energy use. No placebo group, so clinical effects could not be judged.

NCT03693781.summary: Co-ALS (54 patients): the number of responders did not differ significantly from placebo (5 of 18 on the low dose vs 2 of 18, p=0.22). Functional decline was slower on the low dose (p=0.011). Colchicine was safe.

NCT03792490.summary: ROCK-ALS (120 patients): 4 weeks of intravenous fasudil was safe and well tolerated, its primary endpoint. No clear effect on efficacy measures; a post hoc analysis suggested slower spread to new muscles.

NCT03359538.summary: Rapamycin (63 patients) did not reach its primary endpoint, an increase in regulatory T cells; it was well tolerated and lowered some inflammation markers.

NCT03019419.summary: Perampanel (66 patients) was harmful at 8 mg: function declined 8.4 points more than on placebo (p=0.015), mainly in speech and swallowing, with more serious adverse events.

NCT02868580.summary: Lighthouse (40 patients): long-term Triumeq was safe and well tolerated, with a suggestive 22% slower decline. The phase 3 Lighthouse II was later stopped for futility.

NCT04762589.summary: RT001 (43 patients) was safe and well tolerated; function at 24 weeks favoured RT001 by 1.9 points, not significant (p=0.25).

NCT04165850.summary: Open-label (16 patients): PrimeC (ciprofloxacin plus celecoxib) was safe and well tolerated, leading to the PARADIGM phase 2b.

NCT03204500.summary: Valproate plus lithium (43 patients): decline was slower than on placebo (0.51 vs 1.20 points a month between months 6 and 14), but many dropped out, especially on placebo; the authors call for a larger trial.

NCT03618966.summary: Proof-of-concept (22 patients): magnetic stimulation of one arm's muscles preserved strength compared with sham stimulation of the other arm.

NCT01854294.summary: Pilot (12 patients): the company-authored report describes favourable changes in blood biomarkers and breathing vs placebo; too small to judge efficacy.

NCT00635960.summary: Growth hormone (40 patients) had no effect on a brain-imaging marker or on functional decline over 12 months.

NCT00355576.summary: Selection trial (86 patients): celecoxib plus creatine was chosen over minocycline plus creatine for further testing; neither was compared with placebo.

NCT00244244.summary: Arimoclomol at up to 300 mg a day was well tolerated and safe (dose-ranging study, 80 patients).

NCT00140452.summary: Open-label thalidomide (23 patients): no improvement in function or breathing compared with historical controls, and several side effects.

NCT00072709.summary: TCH346 (591 patients) did not slow functional decline or improve survival, breathing or strength.

NCT00230074.summary: Long-term extension of the TCH346 trial, which found no benefit.

NCT02794857.summary: NP001 phase 2. A 2024 pooled, post hoc analysis of the NP001 trials reported longer survival at 2 mg/kg (hazard ratio 0.77, p=0.07), mainly in patients aged 65 or under.

NCT01281631.summary: NP001 phase 2 (136 patients). A 2024 pooled, post hoc analysis of the NP001 trials reported longer survival at 2 mg/kg (hazard ratio 0.77, p=0.07), mainly in patients aged 65 or under.

NCT03114215.summary: High-dose biotin MD1003 (30 patients): safe and well tolerated, with no significant difference in function at 6 months (p=0.49).

NCT02487407.summary: LEVALS: oral levosimendan did not improve breathing capacity measured sitting, its primary endpoint; a post hoc analysis favoured it lying down, which the REFALS phase 3 then failed to confirm.

NCT01879241.summary: Rasagiline added to riluzole (252 patients) did not improve survival; a post hoc analysis suggested possible benefit in faster-progressing patients.

NCT01777646.summary: Phase 2a of NurOwn (14 patients): safe, with slower decline after treatment than before (uncontrolled). The phase 3 later missed its primary endpoint.

NCT01277315.summary: Anakinra (17 patients) was safe and lowered inflammatory markers at first, but did not slow progression vs historical controls; most patients developed antibodies against it.
